title: Pull a Christmas cracker with both hands until it cracks and parts, then put the pieces down
instruction: Pull the Christmas cracker with both hands until it cracks, then put the pieces down.
context: Pulling crackers is part of Christmas dinner in Britain and much of the Commonwealth: about 150 million are pulled in the UK each Christmas (a consumer survey widely reported in the UK press). Two people, or one person with both hands, each take an end and pull until a crimp tears and the snap goes off; whoever keeps the middle gets the hat and the gift. Each hand must hold its end firmly enough not to slip as the pull builds, and the two must pull against each other along the cracker: one hand alone only drags it about.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); the layout is the same in every trial. Loose: a standard 12 in Christmas cracker (red foil paper over a card tube; 30 cm long, 5 cm across, crimped with gold bands to about 2.4 cm 7.5 cm either side of its middle; about 40 g, with a paper hat, a joke and a small boxed gift inside) lying across the table, its middle at x 30, y 0, its length along y (ends at y -15 and +15). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Checked at the end. 1.0: cracked (an end torn off the middle at its crimp, more than 10 mm apart), every piece down on the table, no part of either gripper within 2 cm of any piece, all still, for 1 s. 0.5: cracked, the pieces not yet down and let go. 0.25: held up off the table by both ends (both more than 3 cm up), not cracked. 0: anything else (for example still whole, or dragged whole by one hand).
reset_notes: Clear away the pieces, the hat, the joke and the gift, and lay a new cracker across the table at the marked spot. The cracker is consumed (about £1).
fidelity: The crimps tear by force, with no rules: each end is held to the middle by a PhysX fixed joint that breaks past its tearing force (20 N on one side, 18 N on the other) or 0.25 N m of bending, so the arms must pull that hard through their grip. Tearing forces, masses and frictions are our estimates (no published pull force); sizes are a standard 12 in cracker's. Rigid tubes (it cannot be crushed); no bang. Boxes.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both hands go to the cracker's ends and stay over them; it never grips and pulls); demo: 1.0 (success at step 312)
